key_insight: Fair bandwidth tuning matters more than the observed quantum–classical accuracy differences, with tuned quantum kernels statistically indistinguishable from tuned RBF kernels on four real datasets.
engineering_relevance: Quantum-kernel evaluations should use matched tuning budgets, fold-specific preprocessing and kernel recomputation, and hardware circuit counts rather than simulator runtime.
method: Match quantum bandwidth and classical kernel tuning budgets.
Refit preprocessing and recompute kernels within every fold.
Evaluate 324 factorial-design cells, four real datasets, noise ablations, and a circuit-cost sweep.
evidence_signal: Bandwidth tuning improved accuracy by 0.120 on synthetic data and 0.339 on real data; synthetic quantum advantages occurred almost entirely on data generated by the feature map itself.
watch_item: Hardware scaling remains a concern: a fidelity kernel requires about 50 million circuit evaluations at 10,000 samples, and finite-shot sampling degraded accuracy more than gate and readout noise.
paper_title: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Classification: A Comparative Study with Classical Kernels
